selection: Toulouse to win the match (Win Match / moneyline)
text: Back Toulouse to win at Ernest-Wallon. The champions of France sit top of the Top 14 on 24 points from six rounds, five wins and a +73 points difference, and they have scored freely all month: 45-34 over Bayonne in round six with Antoine Dupont crossing twice, then 43-40 against Exeter Chiefs to open their Champions Cup campaign. Perpignan, ninth on 13 points and minus 33 for the season, needed a late Luke McGrath try to put away a Vannes side that is still without a win. Toulouse will be without the injured Thomas Ramos and Tommaso Menoncello, but Blair Kinghorn has been cleared and Jack Willis is close to returning, so the depth at half-back and in the back three still dwarfs what Perpignan can field on the road. Selection: Toulouse on the moneyline. Our handicap line has them giving 14.5 points.

selection: Afghanistan to win the match (Win Match / moneyline)
text: Take Afghanistan to win this one. They are rated 92 to Bangladesh's 82 in the ICC men's ODI rankings, and the gap on the field has been far wider than that all week: Afghanistan beat Bangladesh by 200 runs in the second ODI, bowling them out for 109 in pursuit of 191, having already thumped Zimbabwe by 158 runs behind Sediqullah Atal's 102 from 110 balls and Ibrahim Zadran's 90. Rahmat Shah's side top the tri-series table on net run rate of +3.160, while Bangladesh are still pointless at minus 1.980 and, on the tournament's own maths, need a big win plus other results to reach Friday's final. Litton Das has carried the batting with 155 runs, but that is not enough cover for a collapse-prone middle order. Selection: Afghanistan on the moneyline.
